title: The later Kirby band, the bass clarinet and personnel losses
summary: Later years used tenor players; Kirby bought a bass clarinet around 1939; losing three of five hurt the sextet.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

There's also a quote, I think, attributed to John Kirby around -- sometime around the beginning of the war -- where he discusses his plans for the sextet. He said that the next thing he would like to do would be to augment it by adding someone who played flute and baritone sax.

Well, Kirby actually bought a bass clarinet. And he was practicing the bass clarinet he was going to add. Because on one of my albums, -- not albums, on an early record, -- "Easy To Love," where Claude had made an arrangement, and Claude used a bass clarinet on there. There's a run in there if you listen closely -- there's a bass clarinet passage. So Kirby liked the instrument, and he went out and bought a bass clarinet.

In fact, for a while, maybe about a month, he did have a bass clarinetist sitting in the orchestra at the Onyx Club. I forget his name, but there is a photograph somewhere with Kirby's orchestra, and this young man is sitting in the band. He's playing bass clarinet.
So I -- oh, I'm sure --
Do you remember when that was?
Oh, it had to be probably '39 in those days, because I left the band when I went out to Hollywood.
I came back and worked with him on one or two engagements. Then I was no longer affiliated with the band, except when we had the Flow Gently Sweet Gently Show.
I was going off in another direction.
